Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Two quick questions the compliance team asked me to put in writing so we have a record:

1) When we "pin" our Dedicated environment to an EU region, does that pin extend to all persistent backups and snapshots (managed by Redwood) or only to the live serving/replica cluster? In other words, could a backup snapshot ever be stored outside the pinned region?

2) We have an escrow/retention policy requirement where an independent escrow vendor might store a copy of encrypted data for archive/DR. If we agree to an escrow arrangement, does Redwood provide an export package that is region-scoped (i.e., the escrow copy will also be EU-resident)?

We'd prefer short, explicit answers we can forward to Legal. If helpful, please include any attachment that shows the data flow.

Elena —

Short answers up front:
- Pinning (region-binding) applies to all customer-controlled persistent storage managed by Redwood for Dedicated: live replicas, persistent volumes, and point-in-time snapshots. Redwood will not store those artifacts outside the pinned region.
- Escrow exports: Redwood can produce an export bundle that is restricted to the same region you pin; the bundle is encrypted client-side (customer-managed key if requested) before transfer to an escrow vendor. The escrow copy can be delivered to an EU-hosted escrow provider per contract.

Detail:
- What we pin: when you request region-binding for a Dedicated tenant, orchestration ensures scheduling, persistent volume provisioning, and snapshot storage are constrained to an allowed set of AZs within the selected region. This is enforced at the scheduler and storage orchestration layers; metadata for the snapshots includes region tags and the snapshot storage class is region-local.
- Backups & snapshot lifecycle: automatic snapshots (user-configurable cadence) are kept in the same region. Cross-region replication is not enabled unless explicitly requested in the tenant config.
- Escrow workflow: we produce an encrypted export (tar.gz) containing the dataset and metadata manifest, signed and checksummed. By default the export is encrypted with a Redwood-managed key; if you require escrow with key separation, we support a customer-supplied KMS/HSM key to encrypt the package client-side. The exported bundle can either be staged in your EU-only staging bucket (we will not transfer it outside the EU) or pushed directly to an escrow vendor endpoint you provide that is EU-hosted.

I've attached a simplified dataflow diagram and the export manifest template to show what fields are included.

Next steps: if Legal wants, we can produce a short attestation letter and a sample DocuSign envelope for the escrow transfer.

—Ben

Elena —

Adding a couple operational guardrails you can include in your acceptance criteria:

• Retention windows: snapshots and backups inherit the tenant retention policy. If you ask for a 90-day retention, we won't purge before 90 days unless there's an approved legal hold or you initiate deletion.
• Legal hold / preservation: placing a preservation order will freeze scheduled purges for the affected tenant ID; purge jobs will skip items with the hold tag. We can provide a CSV report of objects under hold (name, snapshot id, created_at).
• Backup escrow verification: Redwood supports a verification step where the escrow vendor posts a signed receipt and checksums back to the tenant's compliance S3 endpoint; we can automate checksum validation and keep logs for audit (retained per your SLA).

If NovaBank Legal needs formal wording for the SOC/SLA, we can draft the paragraph and include it in the Master Services Schedule.

Thanks,
Laura

Hi Elena —

Answers to your follow-ups (A/B/C):

A) KMS/key separation: confirmed. If you supply the customer-managed key (CMK) and we perform client-side envelope encryption, Redwood will not have the plaintext nor the CMK. Our export path supports either:
   - Customer-side encrypt & upload: your tooling encrypts the bundle and you push to the escrow endpoint; Redwood processes the transfer as opaque bytes.
   - Redwood-assisted export with customer CMK: Redwood uses the CMK via a temporary, audited KMS grant that you control; the grant is narrow and logged, and we automatically revoke the grant after encrypting the bundle. Under either pattern, plaintext is never persisted on Redwood-managed long-term storage.

B) Metadata exposure: the escrow bundle contains a manifest with object IDs, size, checksums, and a minimal schema map required for restore. No raw customer data is left unencrypted. If you require, we can redact the object name fields and provide canonical IDs only; vaulting/restore is still possible using the canonical map plus your private index. We can also scope the manifest to exclude business-meaningful filenames.

C) Timeline: we can produce a short attestation + DocuSign envelope template within 48 business hours. I'll attach a draft attestation and the DocuSign link (sample). If Legal needs different phrasing, we can iterate quickly — typical turnaround for final sign-off is 3–7 business days depending on changes.

Attachments: pin-attestation-docusign.pdf (sample attestation), resident-architecture.pdf (for reference).

Action items we propose:
1) You confirm preferred escrow pattern (customer-side encrypt vs Redwood-assisted with CMK).
2) We share an EU endpoint for staging the export.
3) We provide the attestation and DocuSign sample for Legal review (48 business hours).

I'll be available for a short call CET afternoon if you want to walk through.
